chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: Charlie Parker as a person and dinner at his mother's in Kansas City
summary: Parker was brilliant and a nice man; Jones remembers dinner at his mother's house during Jazz at the Philharmonic.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: What was he like then as a person?
Fine. Nice cat. Very nice man.
He was a very brilliant man, wasn't he?

Yes, he was. I had dinner at his house in Kansas City once. We were doing Jazz at the Philharmonic, and I met his mother, and his mother was like a typical mother. You know, her son could do no wrong. And she fixed -- oh, boy, she fixed a great meal for us. Sarah Vaughan, George Treadwell, Dexter Gordon, we all went by there and had dinner, you know?
She treated us like we were her children. You know, that kind of feeling, a very warm feeling in the house, you know?

Well, Charlie Parker was -- when you said the word brilliant, he was a brilliant man. Because he could talk about so many different things, you know, not just the music. But he could really expound on a lot of stuff.
Can you remember any of the subjects that he talked about?
